Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Health Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for those wishing to ask a question will be given later. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Health Partners' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are David Harper, Chief Executive Officer; Rachel Kim, Chief Financial Officer; and Mark Ellis, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Harper.

David Harper:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

During the quarter, we admitted over 150,000 patients across our 45-hospital footprint, with adjusted patient days up 5.2% year-over-year, driven by strong elective procedure recovery in orthopedics and cardiology, as well as sustained demand in our behavioral health continuum. Our hospitals achieved top-decile quality scores under CMS's Star Ratings, with readmission rates 15% below national benchmarks, thanks to our integrated post-acute partnerships. We also opened two new micro-hospitals in high-growth Texas MSAs through JVs with physician groups, adding 50 beds focused on outpatient high-acuity services.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on four key aspects: payer mix optimization, initiatives to improve operating margin, supply costs and other operating expenses management, and operating margin performance by segment.

On payer mix, we maintained a diversified portfolio that buffered reimbursement volatility while growing commercial volumes. Our margin improvement efforts yielded meaningful progress through throughput enhancements and revenue cycle gains. We exercised strong discipline on supply costs amid inflation, and our segments delivered resilient profitability.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Rachel to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Rachel Kim:
Thank you, David. Good morning, everyone. As David mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $3.25 billion, an increase of 6.8% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, a favorable payer shift, and improved case mix.

Let me start by unpacking our payer mix, which remains a cornerstone of our revenue stability and growth strategy in the dynamic healthcare services and hospitals sector. Our diversified payer portfolio continues to shield us from reimbursement volatility while positioning us to capitalize on favorable demographic tailwinds and value-based care opportunities.

For the third quarter, our net revenue payer mix broke down as follows: Medicare accounted for 41.2% of total net revenue, Medicaid contributed 17.8%, commercial insurance and managed care payers made up 36.5%, and self-pay plus other sources represented 4.5%. This compares to Q3 2023, when the split was Medicare at 43.1%, Medicaid at 16.2%, commercial at 35.4%, and self-pay/other at 5.3%. On a year-to-date basis through Q3 2024, the mix stands at Medicare 42.0%, Medicaid 18.1%, commercial 35.2%, and self-pay/other at 4.7%—a modest shift that reflects our deliberate strategies to optimize commercial capture while navigating payer-specific headwinds.

Medicare, our largest revenue source at over 41% this quarter, saw volume grow 4.2% year-over-year, fueled by the aging Baby Boomer cohort—now representing 28% of our inpatient admissions, up from 25% last year—and sustained post-acute demand in our skilled nursing and home health continuum. However, this growth was tempered by CMS's FY2025 IPPS final rule, which delivered only a 2.8% payment update after adjustments for productivity and wage index factors, landing below our expectations amid ongoing productivity adjustment recoupments totaling $1.2 billion industry-wide. Our Medicare case mix index held steady at 1.78, benefiting from our clinical documentation improvement program, which leverages AI-powered tools from 3M and Nuance to capture HCCs and SOI/ROM accuracy. Regionally, our Midwest markets—such as our Ohio and Michigan hospitals—saw Medicare mix exceed 48%, driven by rural designation premiums, while our Sunbelt expansions in Texas and Florida moderated to 38% due to higher commercial density.

Medicaid's 17.8% share marked a 9.7% year-over-year volume increase, primarily from redetermination unwind in non-expansion states like Texas and Georgia, where we operate 14 facilities. Post-PHE unwinding, we've stabilized collections at 92% of billed charges, up from 87% last year, thanks to our state-specific supplemental payment strategies aligned with the Medicaid Directed Payment Programs. In expansion states like our Pennsylvania and California clusters, Medicaid now comprises 22% of revenue, bolstered by 1115 waiver extensions for behavioral health and SDOH initiatives. We're prudently managing acuity shifts, with Medicaid CMI improving to 1.45 via targeted ED diversion programs that reduce low-acuity boarding.

Commercial insurance and managed care, at 36.5%, delivered the strongest growth, with net revenue up 8.1% year-over-year on 6.4% volume gains and 1.7% net rate improvement. This reflects successful renegotiations with majors like UnitedHealthcare, Anthem, and Cigna, where we've locked in mid-teens unit growth contracts emphasizing bundled payments for ortho, cardio, and maternity episodes—mirroring strategies seen at peers like HCA Healthcare in high-commercial acuity markets. Our outpatient shift is key here: ambulatory surgery centers and hospital outpatient departments now capture 42% of commercial volume, at reimbursement rates 20-30% above inpatient DRGs, aided by the No Surprises Act's balance billing protections. Regionally, Northeast urban hubs like our New York and Massachusetts facilities hit 45% commercial mix, leveraging narrow networks and direct contracting with employers via our ApexDirect platform.

Self-pay and other, at 4.5%, continues to trend down from 5.3% last year, a positive for margins as we convert uninsured to insured via expanded charity care eligibility under the 340B framework and front-end screening with ClearBalance tools. Uninsured rates stabilized at 6.2% of encounters, below the AHA's national 7.8% average, with self-pay collections at 28% of charges—bolstered by our revenue cycle management tech stack, including Waystar for claims scrubbing, which reduced denials to 4.1% from 5.6%.

Strategically, we're focused on payer diversification to counter CMS's site-neutral payment pressures and Medicaid budget squeezes. Key initiatives include scaling our ACO REACH participation—now covering 15% of Medicare lives, generating $28 million in shared savings—and piloting downside risk contracts with Humana and Centene for dual-eligible SNPs. We've invested $45 million in Epic-integrated prior authorization automation, slashing commercial denial overturns by 22%, and are expanding value-based reimbursements to 28% of total revenue by year-end, targeting commercial payers with our ortho bundles at 15% below fee-for-service. Regionally, we're tilting capex toward high-commercial growth corridors like the Southeast, where Medicaid expansion momentum and employer migration from states like New York bolster upside.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 payer mix stability with Medicare at 41-42%, Medicaid 17-18%, commercial 36-37%, and self-pay under 5%, assuming no major CMS sequesters. This positions us for 5-7% net revenue growth in FY2025, outpacing peers like Tenet and Community Health Systems amid favorable acuity trends.

Our operating expenses were $2.85 billion, representing 87.7% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives. This contributed to our consolidated operating margin expanding 120 basis points year-over-year to 11.2%, marking the strongest quarterly performance in our same-facility portfolio since pre-pandemic levels. This improvement reflects early payoffs from our multi-year margin expansion playbook, executed with discipline amid industry headwinds like persistent labor inflation and reimbursement pressures from Medicare's 2.9% IPPS cut effective FY2024.

Let me outline the key initiatives driving this momentum, centered on our three-pillar strategy: operational efficiency, revenue cycle optimization, and cost discipline. Our goal is sustainably delivering 14-16% operating margins by FY2026—putting us in the upper quartile of acute care peers like HCA and Community Health Systems.

First, operational efficiency: We're prioritizing throughput and productivity to drive same-facility volume growth without proportional fixed cost increases. In Q3, we reduced average length of stay by 4.2% across our 45-hospital footprint to 4.1 days, ahead of our internal target of 4.3 days. This was powered by our proprietary FlowCore initiative, which leverages real-time bed management software integrated with our Epic EHR platform. In high-volume facilities like our Southeast cluster, surgical case volume grew 7% year-over-year, with OR utilization hitting 68%, up from 62% a year ago. We're targeting 72% by year-end through block scheduling optimizations and partnerships with high-acuity surgical groups. Regionally, this shines in our Sunbelt markets—Florida and Texas, which represent 55% of our beds—where elective procedure volumes surged 12% amid strong population in-migration and lower payer mix drag. Conversely, in the Northeast (20% of beds), where we're battling higher unionized labor costs, we've piloted AI-driven predictive analytics to cut ER boarding hours by 22%, unlocking $15 million in annualized capacity value.

Second, revenue cycle management: Enhancing capture and collections to offset flat-to-down reimbursements. Our denial rate dropped to 7.8% from 11.2% year-over-year, thanks to our RevCore AI platform—a machine learning tool co-developed with 3M's coding suite—that automates clinical documentation improvement queries. This boosted our case mix index by 2.1% to 1.85, particularly in cardiology and orthopedics DRGs. Net revenue per admission rose 3.5% to $14,200, driven by a 150 basis point shift in payer mix toward commercial (now 48%) from Medicaid (down to 18%). We've also accelerated cash collections, with days in AR improving to 42 from 48, generating $220 million in incremental free cash flow year-to-date. Looking ahead, we're expanding this to value-based care contracts, where our 15 MSSP ACOs delivered 4.2% savings share, and we're negotiating upside risk models with UnitedHealthcare for 10 new markets in 2025.

Third, cost discipline: Taming labor and supplies, which comprise 60% of our OpEx. On labor, agency and premium pay peaked at 12% of total RN hours in Q1 2023 but fell to 4.1% in Q3, a 250 basis point sequential improvement. This saved $85 million year-over-year, achieved via our TalentCore program: internal travel teams, visa-sponsored LPN pipelines from the Philippines (adding 1,200 FTEs), and productivity metrics tied to 85th percentile benchmarks from Vizient's database. Total labor as a percentage of revenue declined 180 basis points to 48.5%.

These initiatives are integrated via our MarginMax Dashboard, a custom Tableau analytics tool tracking 50+ KPIs in real-time across facilities. Post-COVID, we're capitalizing on easing RN shortages (national vacancy rates down to 12%) and ambulatory migration—growing outpatient revenue 15% year-over-year via 12 new micro-hospitals in JV with private equity partners. Risks include potential CMS site-neutral cuts pressuring outpatient margins by 200-300 basis points, so we're hedging with a 20% ambulatory shift by 2026. Regionally, Midwest facilities face higher bad debt from Medicaid redeterminations, but our charity care optimization keeps it under 3%.

In summary, Q3's 11.2% margin underscores our execution. We guide FY2024 same-facility operating margin to 11.5-12.0%, with Q4 acceleration from seasonal volumes and flu season upside. Our $500 million in capex supports this, with 60% allocated to high-ROI tech like tele-ICU expansions.

Diving deeper into supply costs and other operating expenses, which together represented 42% of our total operating expenses in the quarter, or about $1.2 billion on a consolidated basis. While we saw persistent inflationary pressures, our proactive supply chain strategies delivered supply costs as a percentage of net patient revenue at 27.2%—a 40 basis point improvement year-over-year and ahead of our guided range.

Supply costs clocked in at $482 million for the quarter, up 4.2% on a reported basis from last year. Excluding the impact of 2.5% inpatient volume growth and a 1.1% increase in case mix index—driven by stronger surgical volumes in ortho and neuro—this reflects underlying cost inflation of about 1.8%. Supply intensity was $1,420 per adjusted patient day, flat sequentially but up 2% year-over-year.

Pharmaceutical supplies, 38% of total supply spend at $183 million, rose 6.8% year-over-year, primarily from oncology drug inflation on items like Keytruda and Opdivo analogs, running at 8-10% amid list price hikes from Merck and Bristol Myers Squibb, coupled with higher utilization in our 12 NCI-designated cancer centers. GLP-1 agonists like Ozempic and Mounjaro saw demand surge 15% in bariatrics programs, though offset by 340B pricing. Our hospital-owned outpatient infusion centers captured 25% more volume under value-based contracts with payers like UnitedHealthcare.

Medical device and implant costs, 32% of supply spend or $154 million, rose 3.1% to $892 per surgical case. Orthopedic implants from Stryker and Zimmer Biomet were up 4% due to premium product mix shifts toward robotic-assisted procedures—da Vinci Xi adoption at 85% in eligible cases—but mitigated through direct contracting, shaving 2-3% off list prices. Cardiovascular devices like stents and TAVR valves from Medtronic and Edwards Lifesciences grew 2%, thanks to semiconductor supply normalization. Non-sterile supplies like linens and nutrition, 30% of spend, rose just 1.5% as commodity prices eased.

Regionally, Southeast markets—Florida, Georgia, Carolinas, 60% of bed capacity—saw supply costs per adjusted patient day 5% higher than Midwest due to prior hurricane disruptions inflating freight for PPE and IV fluids. Midwest facilities in Ohio and Indiana benefited from lower regional drug pricing under state Medicaid rebates, keeping pharma inflation to 5% versus 8% in Southeast.

Strategic initiatives include our Vizient GPO partnership, delivering $28 million in savings through their ASCEND platform, including bundled pricing on high-volume items like BD catheters and Baxter IV solutions. We expanded RFPs for 15 SKUs, standardizing to single-source vendors, reducing variance by 18%. AI-powered procurement via GHX's marketplace forecasts shortages—like recent saline issues—and optimizes inventory, cutting carrying costs 11% to $42 million annually. Clinician-led value analysis committees rejected 22% of new device requests based on total cost of care. 340B eligible purchases grew 9% to $112 million.

Other operating expenses totaled $718 million, up 5.5% year-over-year or 3.2% inflation-adjusted after volumes and 1,200 net new FTEs. Salaries, wages, and benefits—62% or $446 million—rose 6.2% from 3.8% merit increases, travel nurse premiums at 2% of RN pool (down from 12%), and rising health plan costs. RN turnover improved to 14.2% from 18% via our Bridge to Bedside retention program, though Midwest union contracts added wage inflation.

Professional fees and purchased services, 18% or $129 million, up 4.8% from outsourced coding for HCC capture with Medicare Advantage (32% of payer mix) and $8 million in cybersecurity legal fees post-Change Healthcare issues. Facilities and utilities rose 7.1% to $92 million from 12% higher natural gas in Southeast and $15 million deferred maintenance like HVAC upgrades. IT and telecom grew 9% to $51 million for Epic MyChart and $75 million ambient AI scribing via Nuance, boosting productivity 22%.

We're targeting 150-200 basis points of OpEx margin expansion via zero-based budgeting, lab consolidations, and IoT energy sensors—piloted in five Florida hospitals for 15% utility savings. Midwest facilities are 10% more efficient on facilities due to newer LEED builds versus older Southeast assets.

Looking ahead, Q4 supply costs rise mid-single digits on volumes but hold flat to down 20 basis points as percentage of revenue, assuming 6% drug inflation moderation. Other OpEx grows 4-5% with occupancy leverage toward 68%.

Finally, on operating margins by segment, our consolidated margin for Q3 was 8.4%, up 130 basis points year-over-year from 7.1% and 40 basis points sequentially from Q2's 8.0%. This marks our sixth straight quarter of expansion, driven by case mix index uplift to 1.82 from 1.75, elective procedure recovery, and cost management like 15% agency nurse reduction via our in-house staffing and VitaFlex Travel Nurse program.

Acute Care Hospitals (76% of revenue, $2.4 billion): Delivered 7.2% margin, up 160 basis points year-over-year. Admissions grew 4.2% to 145,000, patient days up 3.8% on higher acuity—surgical CMI at 2.15 from 12% ortho/cardio growth. Payer mix: 52% Medicare, 28% commercial, 15% Medicaid. Offset CMS 340B clawbacks ($18 million) with 4.5% commercial rate hikes. Cost levers: 8% implant savings via Vizient, 10% LOS reduction to 4.6 days via Epic predictive analytics, cutting readmissions 14%. Sunbelt (45% of segment) led at 8.9% margins; Northeast at 6.1% due to NY staffing mandates ($25 million labor).

Ambulatory Surgery Centers and Outpatient Services (14% of revenue, $450 million): 22.6% margins, up 210 basis points. Revenue per case up 6.8% to $2,450 on procedure migration—28% shift for cataracts, colonoscopies, pain. 120 ASCs saw 9% volume to 185,000 cases. AI coding improved denials to under 4%. California ASCs at 25.2% (65% commercial); Midwest at 19.8%. Targeting 25%+ via five new ASCs in Phoenix/Dallas.

Behavioral Health Facilities (10% of revenue, $320 million): 10.1% margins, down 50 basis points year-over-year but up QoQ. Inpatient days up 7.1% to 210,000 on 22% adolescent/geriatric surge, 92% occupancy. Commercial mix to 35%, 5.2% rate growth. TeleBH scaled virtual programs to 15,000 patients, +300 bps EBITDA via leverage. ShiftWizard cut overtime 18%; Optum bundles for depression/SUD aim for 12% by year-end.

Across segments, our right-site, right-service strategy shifts low-acuity to ASCs/outpatient. $150 million FY24 capex for robotics/digital twins targets 100-150 bps expansion. Guide full-year to 8.5-8.8%, with elective upside.

Net income for the quarter was $285 million, or $1.28 per diluted share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to David.

David Harper:
Thank you, Rachel. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for queuing questions: Press star then one on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from John Smith with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of CMS IPPS updates and Medicare reimbursement changes on your operations?

David Harper:
Thanks for the question, John. As Rachel detailed, the FY2025 IPPS final rule's 2.8% update, after productivity and wage adjustments, came in below expectations, compounded by industry-wide $1.2 billion recoupments. We've mitigated this through our CDI program with 3M and Nuance AI, holding CMI at 1.78, and ACO REACH scaling to 15% of Medicare lives for $28 million savings. In Midwest rural sites, premiums help, while Sunbelt commercial density balances it. Overall, it tempers volume growth but our payer diversification keeps us on track for 5-7% FY2025 revenue growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Davis with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Davis:
What are your expectations for patient volume growth in the next quarter, considering the current environment?

Rachel Kim:
Good question, Emily. We expect Q4 same-facility admissions growth of 4-6%, building on Q3's 4.2%, driven by seasonal flu/RSV uptick, continued elective rebound (ortho/cardio +10-12%), and behavioral health demand. Sunbelt in-migration supports 12% procedure surge there. We'll leverage FlowCore for ALOS under 4.1 days and OR utilization to 72%, with ambulatory shift adding outpatient days. Risks like site-neutral proposals are hedged by our 42% commercial outpatient capture at premium rates.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez:
Thanks. On supply costs, how are you managing pharma inflation and device pricing into next year?

Rachel Kim:
Mike, pharma remains challenging at 6-8% inflation for oncology/GLP-1s, but Vizient ASCEND and GHX AI have locked $28 million savings, with clinician committees rejecting 22% requests. Direct contracting shaves 2-3% on ortho implants, and 340B growth to $112 million helps. We expect flat percentage in Q4 via standardization and inventory optimization, outperforming peers as volumes leverage fixed costs toward 68% occupancy.

David Harper:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Health Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
